nodes.title: Plaza Pyramids: Function & Access
nodes.narrative_description: The expert is positioned on the plaza of Cowgill Hall, observing four distinctive pyramids. These structures serve to both demarcate the center of the plaza and act as functional skylights for the underground Burchard extension. The plaza itself is conceptually divided into quadrants, with each typically featuring an entrance to Burchard, although one entrance is specifically noted as absent near Cowgill's main entry. The expert's active left hand likely aids in pointing out these features during the detailed explanation of the plaza's design and hidden complexities.

nodes.title: Plaza to Cowgill Transition
nodes.narrative_description: The expert observes a critical transitional space, highlighting specific demarcations defining the area. Immediately to their right, an elevator and mechanical facilities occupy a distinct zone. Another clear boundary visually separates the plaza's termination from the commencement of Cowgill Hall. This location is significant for its functional infrastructure and architectural separation of distinct public areas, as the expert explains these delineating features.

nodes.title: Bridge, Vestibule, Mirrored Wall
nodes.narrative_description: The expert describes a structural bridge connecting to an underground area, spanning an alley below. They highlight two distinct front doors and an adjacent vestibule area at this transition point. Attention is drawn to the length and capping of a specific wall, whose design is a significant architectural motif. The expert explains this wall's condition is almost a mirrored replicate of one found in the lobby, emphasizing a recurring design theme.

nodes.title: Lobby's Functional Slatted Wall
nodes.narrative_description: The expert describes a distinctive slatted wall design in the school's lobby, noting its unique extension and how it opens into the main space. This integrated system functions as a dynamic "museum" for rotating student exhibitions, explicitly designed to hold standard paper sizes for pinups. Significant wear on the slats underscores its extensive use over many years for displaying student work, critiques, and feedback. The expert also points out the adjacent Dean's and Architecture offices, orienting the viewer within this central hub.

nodes.title: Cowgill Entry, Stairs, Studios
nodes.narrative_description: The expert describes Cowgill's fundamental linear layout, flanked by two doors that lead to fire stairs. These stairs facilitate critical vertical circulation throughout and egress from the building. A prominent front wall in the lobby separates the space into distinct exhibition and studio areas. This location notably features a plethora of studios, including two designated first-year studios.

nodes.title: Lobby Lab Workstation Activity
nodes.narrative_description: The expert identifies bookshelves and a series of tables within a lobby area, configured for collaborative work and exhibits. This versatile space functions as a typical first-year lab, especially during morning hours. Currently, students are observed actively engaged in modeling assignments here. The description highlights the area's dual purpose as a functional workspace and display zone.

nodes.title: Student Lab Model Iterations
nodes.narrative_description: The expert observes a first-year design lab where students are actively modeling various forms derived from drawings. They explain how students explore abstract concepts like curvature, structural integrity, and part interchangeability through iterative paper models. This process translates initial ideas from two-dimensional drawings into tangible, three-dimensional explorations. The expert's detailed descriptions reveal a dynamic learning environment focused on hands-on material application and conceptual design development.

This suggests the stairwell serves a significant aesthetic or functional role beyond simple transit. The expert intends to highlight the grandeur and potential for display within this ground-level area.

nodes.title: Ferrari Archive and Design Labs
nodes.narrative_description: The expert identifies the Ferrari archive, explaining it contains items from Lucio and Olivio Ferrari. Adjacent to this is an industrial design laboratory, which the expert notes is flanked by another similar lab. Their active left hand suggests pointing at these distinct areas. This commentary clarifies the purpose and arrangement of these significant archival and functional spaces.

nodes.narrative_description: The expert describes a small robotics lab, highlighting work done with robot arms, casting, and hot wire cutting techniques. Adjacent to this is the school's 3D printing lab, offering diverse material printing like ceramics, traditional plastics, and filaments. This 3D printing facility is typically staffed by students, providing valuable resources for those without personal printers. The expert's description emphasizes the practical fabrication capabilities and collaborative student environment of these labs.

Adjacent to this area, a 3D printing lab offers various systems for student use, typically staffed by students themselves. The expert is explaining the integrated educational and social infrastructure available to students at this central location.

They describe a direct staircase and flanking ramps that ascend to a mezzanine. This upper level houses various facilities including faculty offices, a wood shop, and a metal shop. Their intent is to explain the architectural features and functional organization of this key entry point.

This central position allows for identifying numerous surrounding academic and technical facilities, including various design and technology labs, classrooms, and faculty offices. Specific noteworthy areas mentioned are the Kiva meeting space, laser cutting room, and the pivotal threshold leading to Cowgill. The expert comprehensively explains both the architectural design and the diverse, interconnected academic functions housed within this prominent campus hub.
